content.comment_body: Here's my scenario: I need to maintain a temperature of 60°C, so I used a threshold switch (on at 0, off at 60). However, when the heating switches off and the temperature drops by 0.1°C, it turns on again immediately. I'd prefer to have the system reach 60°C, and only turn the heating on again if the temperature drops to 59°C, rather than toggling instantly. Is this possible with [product_name]?
That works! Thanks! (Feeling a bit silly now)

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered an issue with rapid toggling of heating due to the absence of hysteresis in the temperature control logic. While [product_name] provides threshold switching functionality, some users may not realize how to add a difference between the on and off points. Community members quickly offered practical guidance, demonstrating that the solution is available within the product’s settings.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to offer options for hysteresis or adjustable control thresholds, so heating can be switched on at 59°C and off at 60°C, avoiding frequent toggling.
